title: The List from Ten Thousand Years Ago
next_chapter_hook: "Just as Chen Ji was on the verge of being crushed by the truth, Su Qingyao's voice sounded again, as light as a feather falling into an abyss——"

text.content: "The outline of the fourth gate's phantom slowly coalesced within the depths of the Tianji Record, like a sword suspended in the heavens, ready to fall at any moment. Chen Ji sat cross-legged in the secret chamber, the spiritual light around him dim, only the fragment mark between his brows glowing with a cold, faint radiance. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul drifted out from the first page, his features blurred like viewing flowers through mist, yet his voice carried unprecedented gravity: 'The Fourth Gate——the Door of the Observer. Are you certain you wish to open it?'"

"Chen Ji gave no answer. His gaze was locked on the newly emerging runes on the fragment page—those ancient characters writhed and twisted like living things, eventually coalescing into a line of text he had never seen before: 'The Register of Observers Across Ten Thousand Years.' His heart hammered in his chest like war drums, and he had an ominous premonition: the thing behind this door would completely change the relationship between him and Su Qingyao."

dialogue.content: "'The Observer... that was the original author of the Tianji Record.' Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul trembled slightly. 'Every Observer left behind a register, recording those whose fates were most entangled with their own. Before the first Observer of ten thousand years ago perished, they too left such a list.'"

text.content: "The runes on the fragment suddenly exploded outward. Countless specks of light drifted like fireflies, converging before Chen Ji's eyes into a hazy image—a ancient altar, and standing at its center, a woman in white robes. Her features were indistinct, but those eyes were so clear they seemed capable of piercing through ten thousand years of time, gazing directly toward where Chen Ji stood."

"The next instant, the image shattered. A scroll of yellowed silk descended from the void, and Chen Ji caught it instinctively. The silk was ice-cold to the touch, covered densely with names, each accompanied by birth dates and fate characteristics. His gaze swept across those unfamiliar names, and his heart suddenly skipped a beat—at the very bottom of the silk, three elegant characters were clearly visible: Su Qingyao."

dialogue.content: "'Impossible...' Chen Ji's voice trembled, his fingertips gripping the silk's edge so hard they went white. 'This list was made ten thousand years ago, how could Qingyao...' Before he could finish, he suddenly recalled the recurring dream Su Qingyao had mentioned—a dream of a woman with an indistinguishable face, identical to herself."

text.content: "Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul drifted closer, his voice deep as an ancient bell: 'The first Observer and their fated one were not ordinary cultivation partners, but beings whose fates and bloodlines were intertwined. Their descendants would inherit part of the Observer's perception abilities, passed down through generations until the bloodline thinned, or until they encountered another Tianji Record inheritor...'"

"Chen Ji abruptly raised his head: 'Are you saying... Qingyao is a descendant of the first Observer? Does she carry the bloodline of the fate-writer?' Mo Xiansheng gave no answer, but that silence itself was the answer. Chen Ji felt his mind buzzing— no wonder Su Qingyao could faintly sense the aura of the Tianji Record, no wonder she had been blocked by some force each of the three times she came close to the truth."

"'Once the Observer's Register appears, it means the gears of fate have already meshed.' Mo Xiansheng's voice carried an imperceptible trace of compassion. 'Those on the list have all been marked by the Observer. Their fates will be entangled with the Tianji Record holder until... one side is completely annihilated.'"

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji rose abruptly, the silk crumpled in his fist. His mind raced: if Qingyao's name is on this list, it means her fate has been bound to mine all along. But does she know? Does she know she was inscribed with this damned mark from the moment she was born?"

text.content: "Just then, three gentle knocks came at the restriction outside the secret chamber—the unique knocking rhythm belonging only to Su Qingyao. Chen Ji froze all over. He looked down at the silk in his hand, then at the vague silhouette beyond the door, and an almost suffocating emotion surged through him. She had arrived too perfectly, as if fate had long arranged this scene."

choice.prompt: "Su Qingyao was waiting outside the door. Chen Ji gripped the silk tightly, his knuckles white. How was he supposed to face this woman whose destiny had been intertwined with his since ten thousand years ago?"

choices.description: "Hand the silk to Su Qingyao and let her see with her own eyes the fact that her name appears on a list from ten thousand years ago. The truth may be cruel, but deception is even more shameful."
choices.risk_hint: "Su Qingyao may be unable to accept that her fate was written long ago"

text.content: "Chen Ji took a deep breath and released the restriction. The instant Su Qingyao pushed the door open, he had already extended the silk toward her: 'Qingyao, there are things... you perhaps should have known long ago.'"

choices.description: "Store the silk deep within the Tianji Record first, covering the异样 with his usualtrash persona. He was unwilling to let her bear this weight of fate, even if he had to carry everything alone."
choices.visible_reward: "Protect Su Qingyao from being hurt by the truth"
choices.risk_hint: "The Tianji Record's aura may already have been sensed by her, and the lie could be exposed at any moment"

text.content: "Chen Ji swept his sleeve, and the silk vanished into the depths of the Tianji Record. He switched to a languid expression and turned to face Su Qingyao entering: 'This late at night, what brings the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow to gracing my humble quarters?'"

choices.description: "Don't directly reveal the list, but start from that recurring dream of hers. Let her speak of what she saw in the dream herself, then slowly guide her to understand the truth."
choices.visible_reward: "Let Su Qingyao accept the truth proactively rather than being a passive recipient"
choices.risk_hint: "If her dream content differs from the list, it may arouse greater suspicion"

text.content: "Chen Ji subtly slipped the silk into his sleeve and turned to face Su Qingyao: 'Senior Sister Su Qingyao, did you have that dream again tonight?'"

dialogue.content: "Su Qingyao stood at the doorway, her moon-white robes shimmering with a soft glow under the corridor lanterns. Her gaze swept across Chen Ji's somewhat pallid face, her brow furrowed: 'Your aura is very chaotic. What happened?'"

text.content: "Chen Ji managed a smile, about to speak, when Su Qingyao suddenly raised her hand to interrupt: 'Stop pretending.' She walked into the secret chamber, casually closing the stone door, her voice lowered considerably, 'On my way here just now, I saw that woman again. She stood in a void and said to me——'The time has come.'"

"Chen Ji's heart plummeted. 'The time has come'—that was exactly the warning the Tianji Record issued when the Observer's Register appeared. He stared into Su Qingyao's clear eyes and suddenly realized something: she was not merely on the list, she was the inheritor specially chosen by the first Observer. The preparations left by that woman from ten thousand years ago had finally been triggered tonight."

dialogue.content: "'Chen Ji.' Su Qingyao called his name softly, her tone carrying a vulnerability never heard before, 'I've had the same dream for seventeen years. The woman in the dream has an indistinguishable face, yet she makes me feel... she is me. Tell me, how much do you actually know?'"

choice.prompt: "Su Qingyao's gaze fixed directly on Chen Ji, awaiting his answer. This time, she gave him no room for circumlocution."

choices.text: "Hand over the silk, let her see it with her own eyes"
choices.description: "Display the ten-thousand-year-old list to her, including the notation 'Fate Entanglement·Fate-Forming Mutualism' beside her name. Let her decide for herself how to face this fate."
choices.risk_hint: "Su Qingyao may completely change her attitude toward Chen Ji because of the truth"

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji slowly withdrew the silk and extended it to Su Qingyao: 'The Register of Observers from ten thousand years ago. You... have been on it all along.' His voice was soft, yet each word rang clear, 'Qingyao, from the moment you were born, our fates have been intertwined.'"

choices.text: "Only mention her lineage, not the list"
choices.description: "Tell her the truth about being a descendant of the first Observer, but conceal the existence of the list. Let her know the origins of her bloodline without having to bear the fact that her fate was written."
choices.visible_cost: "The lie will inevitably be exposed eventually"
choices.risk_hint: "If she later discovers the concealment, it may cause an even greater rift"

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji hesitated for a moment, then spoke softly: 'Qingyao, do you know where your bloodline comes from? Ten thousand years ago, there was an Observer whose perception abilities were passed down through generations, eventually converging in you.'"

text.content: "Su Qingyao's hand trembled slightly as she accepted the silk. When her gaze fell upon her own name, her entire body was struck like by lightning, frozen in place. That line of small text 'Fate Entanglement·Fate-Forming Mutualism' burned her eyes, and also burned through seventeen years of confusion and obsession."

"After a long while, she raised her head, her eyes were red-rimmed yet not a single tear fell: 'So... from the very beginning, the free will I thought I had, the choices I thought I made... were all arranged?' Her voice was soft, yet heavier than any accusation: 'Chen Ji, my care for you, my trust, even those inappropriate thoughts... were all because of this bloodline?'"

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji looked into those red-rimmed eyes, and his chest felt as if something had grabbed it fiercely. He opened his mouth, yet found any excuse would be too pale. In the end, he only said: 'Qingyao, I would rather you hate this bloodline than hate yourself.'"

text.content: "Su Qingyao suddenly smiled, that smile carrying an indescribable bitterness and relief. She folded the silk carefully and returned it solemnly to Chen Ji's hand: 'I understand.' She turned toward the door, but halfway there she stopped, her back to him as she softly asked, 'Chen Ji, I have one more question for you.'"

dialogue.content: "She turned around, moonlight spilling from behind her, shrouding her face in a hazy glow. Her voice was soft, as if afraid to shatter something: 'If the path you choose would cause me to disappear... would you still walk it?'"

text.content: "This question was like a blade, precisely stabbing into Chen Ji's softest place. He fell silent. In the secret chamber, only the sound of each other's breathing remained, along with the low humming emanating from the unopened Fourth Gate deep within the Tianji Record. The gears of fate had already meshed, and he—this always-calculatingtrash disciple—was truly at a loss for the first time."

"Just as Chen Ji was on the verge of being crushed by the silence, Su Qingyao suddenly stepped forward, so close he could smell the faint fragrance in her hair. Her eyes were still red-rimmed, yet the corners of her lips curved into a slight smile: 'Forget it, don't answer.' She raised her hand, her fingertip lightly touching Chen Ji's chest, 'I probably already know the answer.'"

"She withdrew her hand, stepping back two paces, her moon-white skirt sweeping an elegant arc across the stone floor. Just before leaving, she suddenly looked back: 'Chen Ji, regardless of whether this bond is fate or choice——' her voice carried a tremor, yet was utterly resolute, 'I, Su Qingyao, never accept fate.'"

"The stone door closed, and silence returned to the secret chamber. Chen Ji stood alone, gazing at the direction where Su Qingyao had departed, a dull ache spreading somewhere in his chest. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul sighed faintly: 'The Observer's Register has appeared, and the trial of fate... begins its countdown from this moment.' Chen Ji gave no answer. He only slowly unfolded his palm, gazing at the words 'Fate Entanglement·Fate-Forming Mutualism,' and a determination unlike any he had ever shown flickered in his eyes."
